content.thinking:
I'm checking the root-cause claim against the source lines: the cached spend totals stopped updating at A5 while the purchase ledger stayed correct, and account pages were served the stale copies from A6. The source supports that, though the evidence doesn't yet show what stopped the updates.

I'm moving through the remaining claims against the sources: the cause-in-plain-words hedge, the still-at-risk point, and the symptom all check out, and the causal chains hold up too. I'm now looking at whether the "only check" wording about the reconciliation step is fully supported by the files Code-Fix read.

I'm checking the went_well and went_wrong claims against the alert record: the alert listed the disagreeing cache entries and their timing, and it wasn't linked to any on-call incident, so no one was paged. Both line up with the source.

supported.quote: From {A5} the cached spend totals stopped being updated as new purchases were recorded, so the cached copies fell behind the purchase ledger, which stayed correct, and account pages were served those copies from {A6}.
The evidence does not show what stopped the updates.

The saved copies of shoppers' spending totals stopped being updated when new purchases came in, and the account pages likely showed those copies without checking them against the purchases; what stopped the updates is not known.
Nothing was keeping the cached spend figures up to date, so any shopper's figure could go stale again with their next purchase and be shown on their account page.
Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that were behind their purchases
Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that did not match the purchases behind them.
The pages took their spend figures from cached copies that had fallen behind the purchase ledger. The ledger itself was correct and never moved, and only the cached copies were wrong.
From {A5} the cached copies stopped keeping up with new purchases, and nothing was putting them right. The record does not show what stopped the updates, and no change was found that set this off.

Code-Fix read the account page's code in src/io_shop/account_page.py. In that reading, when the cache returns an entry, the page shows that entry's figure without comparing the purchase count stored with it to the shopper's purchases, which the page already has in hand.
In the files Code-Fix read, the only check that treats a count mismatch as a sign of a stale entry is an offline reconciliation check, not on the serving path.

No alert was seen that would catch the cached spend figures no longer being updated. The fault was found only by the check comparing cached figures with the purchases behind them, after the stale copies were already being served.
The alert itself listed which cached figures disagreed and when the copies stopped keeping up, which gave the mitigation an exact list of entries to discard.
Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was asked to look into why the cached figures had stopped being updated.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one
